proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a successful execution of Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser Algorithms 1--2 that uses only selector values in \(H\) and only denominators supported on \(\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:lgs-case-refinement}\), every existential choice in that execution is represented by a finite decidable candidate set in the input-determined machine, and the machine enumerates the set in its fixed canonical order.  Hence, whenever the published branch predicate has a witness, the enumerated set has a least passing witness.  The machine therefore cannot take the associated exhaustion failure and cannot inspect a selector value outside \(H\).

We compare the two executions recursively over their district tasks.  The factor-kernel conclusion of \(\textnormal{lem:lgs-case-refinement}\) applies at each context, computed-closure, fixing, and Algorithm--2 case: after each displayed predicate has passed, the canonically selected machine factor agrees with the corresponding published factor on the normalized compatible image, independently of the valid fixing order.  The same lemma covers the terminal district product and ancestor marginalization.  Induction over the finite published recursion therefore gives
\[
 F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}=F_H^{\mathrm{LGS}}\{O_H^N(\eta)\}
 =T_{a,H}^N(\eta),
 \qquad \eta\in\mathcal I_H,
\tag{1}
\]
where \(F_H^{\mathrm{LGS}}\) denotes any support-licensed successful published output.  The first equality is extensional: no equality of the two executions' syntactic presentations, context choices, or denominator lists is claimed.

Every division actually made by the machine is entered in its step-indexed ledger.  The hypotheses of the theorem place every compatible observed law in the admissible-cell interior, so \(\textnormal{lem:step-indexed-ledger-positivity}\) yields
\[
 O_H(\Theta_H)\subseteq\mathfrak D_H.
\tag{2}
\]
In particular, all divisions used to evaluate the left side of (1) are legal at a compatible law.  For arbitrary \(\theta\in\Theta_H\), put \(\eta=\nu_H(\theta)\).  Normalization equivalence gives
\[
 O_H^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=O_H(\theta),
 \qquad
 T_{a,H}^N\{\nu_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta).
\tag{3}
\]
Substitution of (3) into (1) gives
\[
 F_H\{O_H(\theta)\}=T_{a,H}(\theta),
 \qquad \theta\in\Theta_H.
\tag{4}
\]
Gate reinsertion reverses the normalized context substitutions by \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\).  Equations (1)--(4) therefore also show that the returned circuit is extensionally equal on \(O_H(\Theta_H)\) to every support-licensed published output.  Equation (2) certifies the actual machine divisors, including intermediate divisors later cancelled.  The proof neither equates distinct branch ledgers nor introduces any selector context outside \(H\).

By \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\), the initial state \(\operatorname{init}_H(I)\) is unique and \(\operatorname{next}_I\) is a total deterministic function of the finite input and current state.  By \(\textnormal{lem:nonresidual-progress}\), every reachable state whose result is \(\operatorname{Running}\) and whose selected work task is nonresidual has a unique successor; hence no such state is stuck.

We first prove local soundness.  For \(s\in H\), \(\textnormal{lem:context-construction-soundness}\) identifies the mechanically selected graph \(G[s]\) and the initialized kernel with evaluation of the known selector gates at \(s\), without introducing a value outside \(H\).  For a positive current kernel \(q\), \(\textnormal{lem:truncated-factorization-identity}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{TF}_{\prec}(q,B)
 =\prod_{X\in B}q\{X\mid\operatorname{pre}_{\prec}(X)\},
\tag{1}
\]
with every conditioning denominator equal to its actual marginal.  If the case function has computed a valid sequence \(\pi\), then \(\textnormal{lem:computed-fixing-soundness}\) gives, at every fixing step,
\[
 q^{\mathrm{new}}
 =\frac{q^{\mathrm{old}}}
 {q^{\mathrm{old}}\{W\mid\operatorname{nd}_G(W),\operatorname{fixed}(G)\}},
\tag{2}
\]
together with the corresponding removal of incoming arrowheads and the exact cross-multiplied identity.  No use of (2) precedes computation of a valid sequence.  For a passing Algorithm--2 triple, \(\textnormal{lem:hybrid-kernel-soundness}\) shows that the product in (1), followed by the computed fixing sequence, equals the required district kernel.  When all district factors have returned, \(\textnormal{lem:district-assembly-soundness}\) gives
\[
 \sum_{Y^*\setminus Y}\prod_{D^*}q_{D^*}
 =T_{a,H}^N
\tag{3}
\]
on every compatible normalized model.  Finally, \(\textnormal{lem:step-indexed-ledger-positivity}\) gives strict positivity of every divisor in (1)--(2) on the compatible image.  Thus each displayed cross-multiplication is reversible there, and all context, factorization, fixing, hybrid, factor-storage, and Join transitions preserve the represented observation--target relation.

The residual transition is also sound.  A projection candidate \(P/D\) passes only if the verifier establishes componentwise, modulo the retained constraints,
\[
 D\,t_{a,H}^N-P(o_H^N)=0,
\tag{4}
\]
and every factor of \(D\) is registered as positive.  Evaluating (4) at \(\eta\in\mathcal I_H\) and dividing by \(D\{O_H^N(\eta)\}>0\) proves
\[
 F_H\{O_H^N(\eta)\}=T_{a,H}^N(\eta).
\tag{5}
\]
A contrast candidate passes only if its two rational affine parameter maps satisfy the primitive simplex constraints, the retained equalities, selector mass positive exactly on \(H\), strict positivity of every admissible cell, equality of every coordinate of \(o_H^N\), and a target contrast with nonzero constant sign.  By \(\textnormal{thm:normalization-equivalence}\), gate reinsertion maps both normalized parameters into \(\Theta_H\) and preserves their observation and target maps.  Hence an accepted contrast is a genuine support-exact global twin.  If all residual candidates fail, the machine emits \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\); neither that result nor an LGS failure tag is assigned causal content.

It remains to establish termination.  Give the control phases their declared natural-number codes, ordered so that every listed control successor has a smaller code.  For a task rank \(r_I(\tau)=(n,c,f,k)\), define the ordinal code
\[
 \rho\{r_I(\tau)\}
 =\omega^3n+\omega^2c+\omega f+k<\omega^4.
\tag{6}
\]
Lexicographic descent of \((n,c,f,k)\) is equivalent to descent of (6); hence the task-rank order is well founded.  For a finite work multiset \(M\), define
\[
 \Omega(M)=\mathop{\#\!\sum}_{\tau\in M}
 \omega^{\rho\{r_I(\tau)\}},
\tag{7}
\]
where \(\#\!\sum\) is the finite natural sum.  If one task is removed, or is replaced by finitely many tasks whose ranks are all strictly smaller, the coefficient of the largest affected exponent in the Cantor normal form of (7) decreases, every larger coefficient is unchanged, and all new summands have smaller exponents.  Therefore \(\Omega(M)\) strictly decreases.  This directly proves well-foundedness of the finite-multiset order defining \(\mu_H\).

We now inspect the exhaustive nonresidual cases of \(\operatorname{next}_I\).  A Start task or district split replaces its parent by proper-ambient district children, or by equal-ambient administrative tasks at a lower control level.  Ancestor restriction decreases the random ambient size unless it merely changes phase, in which case it decreases the control level.  A fixing step decreases the number \(f\) of remaining vertices, and its last step invokes a lower-control continuation.  Rejecting an Algorithm--2 candidate decreases \(k\); accepting one enters lower-control hybrid fixing.  Factor storage and completed Join remove work.  Consequently every nonterminal nonresidual successor satisfies
\[
 \mu_H(\zeta_{m+1})<\mu_H(\zeta_m).
\tag{8}
\]
The residual generators produce finite lists from the residual payload.  Their deterministic verification is therefore a terminating finite computation: it returns the first accepted candidate, if one exists, and otherwise returns \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\).

An infinite run would either contain infinitely many nonresidual transitions, contradicting the well-founded strict descent (8), or reach a residual task after finitely many transitions, after which the finite residual verification terminates.  Thus every run is finite.  Its last state cannot be a running nonresidual state by nonresidual progress.  By the exhaustive result tags and the residual rule, its result is exactly one formula, one verifier-accepted global twin, or one \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\).  Determinism makes this endpoint unique.  Equations (1)--(5) establish the required local identities and certificate soundness along the run, while (8) proves the asserted decrease and termination.

We first reduce the graphical cases for the displayed binary input.  In the target LS-SWIG, \(A\) and \(S\) are fixed, while \(W_0\) and \(Z_0\) have no children.  Therefore the random ancestor set of \(Y\) and its only district are
\[
 Y^*=\{Y\},\qquad D^*=\{Y\}.
\tag{1}
\]
In the observed latent projection, the shared root \(U_0\) induces \(A\leftrightarrow Y\), the shared root \(R_0\) induces \(S\leftrightarrow Y\), and the directed edges are \(S\to A\) and \(A\to Y\).  The isolated vertices \(W_0,Z_0\) are fixable.  Neither \(S\) nor \(A\) is fixable while \(S,A,Y\) remain: in each case its district intersects its descendants in more than the vertex itself.  Hence no reachable superset of \(D^*\) can omit \(S\) or \(A\), whereas \(\{S,A,Y\}\) is reachable by fixing \(W_0,Z_0\).  By \(\textnormal{lem:computed-closure-valid-sequence}\), the computed closure is
\[
 C=\{S,A,Y\}\supsetneq D^*.
\tag{2}
\]
Because \(S\in C\), the deterministic case function enters Algorithm 2.

Here \(\operatorname{ch}^*(S)=\{A\}\).  At \(s=0\), \(A\) is laid back and the serious set is empty, so this context supplies no admissible nonempty-serious triple.  At \(\bar s=1\), the known selector gate forces \(A=1\), giving the only possible pair \(Z=\{A\}\), \(z=1\).  The districts of the mechanically constructed LS-SWIG partition their vertex set, so at most one district \(D'\) contains \(D^*\), and the machine computes that district rather than receiving it as data.  For the resulting candidate, the bidirected edge induced by \(R_0\) leaves \(S\) adjacent to \(Y(\bar s)\).  The line-7 conditioning set does not block this length-one path, so the required d-separation fails.  There is no other supported nonempty-serious triple.  Canonical enumeration therefore exhausts and records
\[
 \operatorname{LGSFailA2NoCandidate}(D^*,C),
\tag{3}
\]
then creates the corresponding residual task.  Equations (1)--(3) use only the input graph and current state, as required by \(\textnormal{prop:input-determinacy}\).

We next verify the residual contrast.  Index the four \(A=1\) natural response rows by \((u_0,r_0)=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\), and set
\[
 r=(3/4,1/4,1/4,3/4),
 \qquad d=(-4,-1,0,3).
\tag{4}
\]
After positive common denominators are cleared, the two observation rows affected by these response probabilities form the rational matrix
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&6&3\\1&2&1&2\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{rref}(M)=
 \begin{pmatrix}1&0&11/3&4/3\\0&1&-4/3&1/3\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{5}
\]
The fixed free-column enumeration sets the third free coordinate to zero and the fourth to three, producing \(d\); direct multiplication gives
\[
 Md^{\mathsf T}=0.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus the fixed generator obtains \(d\) by rational row reduction of the residual observation map, rather than receiving a desired contrast.

For a binary response subtable \(f\in\{0,1\}^4\), define
\[
 \pi_0(f)=\prod_{j=1}^4r_j^{f(j)}(1-r_j)^{1-f(j)},
\tag{7}
\]
\[
 \delta(f)=\pi_0(f)\sum_{j=1}^4
 \frac{d_j\{f(j)-r_j\}}{r_j(1-r_j)},
 \qquad
 \pi_b(f)=\pi_0(f)+b\delta(f).
\tag{8}
\]
Keep the \(A=0\) response rows at their baseline law and combine them with (8), thereby obtaining a law on the full finite canonical response tables.  Independence of the four Bernoulli coordinates under \(\pi_0\) gives
\[
 \sum_f\delta(f)=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_f\pi_b(f)f(j)=r_j+bd_j
 \quad(j=1,\ldots,4).
\tag{9}
\]
For each \(f\), the score multiplying \(b\) in (8) is bounded below by
\[
 -\frac{16}{3}-4-12=-\frac{64}{3}.
\tag{10}
\]
Consequently, if \(0<b<1/32\), then
\[
 \pi_b(f)\geq \pi_0(f)\left(1-\frac{64b}{3}\right)
 >\frac13\pi_0(f)>0.
\tag{11}
\]
Equations (9)--(11) prove normalization and strict simplex membership on the rational open box, consistently with canonical-response richness.

The selector and natural-treatment equations give
\[
 \Pr(S=0\mid R_0=0)=\frac23,
 \qquad
 \Pr(S=0\mid R_0=1)=\frac13,
\tag{12}
\]
with the probabilities reversed for \(S=1\), and
\[
 \Pr(A=1\mid U_0=0,S=0)=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \Pr(A=1\mid U_0=1,S=0)=\frac34.
\tag{13}
\]
Since \((U_0,R_0)\) is uniform, the coefficient of \(b\) in the natural-context cell \(\Pr(S=0,A=1,Y=1)\) is
\[
 \frac14\frac23\left\{\frac14(-4)+\frac34(0)\right\}
 +\frac14\frac13\left\{\frac14(-1)+\frac34(3)\right\}=0.
\tag{14}
\]
In the forced context \(S=1,A=1\), that coefficient is
\[
 \frac14\frac13(-4+0)+\frac14\frac23(-1+3)=0.
\tag{15}
\]
No \(A=0\) response row is perturbed.  Equality of each corresponding \(Y=0\) cell follows from its unchanged \((S,A)\) margin and (14)--(15).  Direct finite summation over \(u_0,r_0\in\{0,1\}\), using (12)--(13) and the baseline response probabilities (4), gives in the stipulated order
\[
 \bigl\{p(S,A,Y)\bigr\}
 =(13,11,13,11,24,24)/96.
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(15) make (16) constant throughout the box.  Its smallest entry is \(11/96>0\).  Appending independent fair \(W_0,Z_0\) multiplies every full observed cell by \(1/4\), so the two complete observed laws agree and every admissible cell remains positive.  Equation (12) and the fair law of \(R_0\) give
\[
 \Pr(S=0)=\Pr(S=1)=\frac12,
\tag{17}
\]
so selector support is exactly \(H=\{0,1\}\).

Under \(do(A=1,S=s_{\emptyset})\), the independent pair \((U_0,R_0)\) remains uniform.  From (4) and (9),
\[
 T_b(Y=1)=\frac12+b\frac{-4-1+0+3}{4}
 =\frac12-\frac b2.
\tag{18}
\]
The simplex inequalities (11), observation identities (14)--(16), exact support (17), strict admissible-cell positivity, and the constant nonzero sign in (18) are precisely the residual verifier's acceptance tests.  It therefore accepts the rational-affine pair consisting of the baseline model at \(b=0\) and the perturbed model at \(b\), for every \(0<b<1/32\).  At \(b=1/64\), their targets are respectively
\[
 \frac12
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \frac12-\frac1{128}=\frac{63}{128},
\tag{19}
\]
while (16) and the independent nuisance factors show equality of the complete observed law.  This proves every asserted component of the worked certificate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Prove the converse for every generated \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\) state: a fiber-constant target must have a verifier-encoded rational projection, while a nonconstant target must have a rational-affine support-exact global-twin box.
open_obligations.obstruction: The deterministic task machine reaches residuals without circular scheduling, but finiteness of the fixed candidate generators does not imply their exhaustiveness. The frozen primitives neither exclude an identified residual having only a nonrational algebraic observable representative nor prove that a common signed response-row contrast lifts through every interacting district and observed descendant while preserving exact selector support.
open_obligations.attempted: Reused the established input determinacy, computed closure and valid fixing, local context, truncated-factorization, hybrid and Join identities, denominator induction, multiset termination, successful LGS refinement, binary residual certificate, and ordinary-ID specialization. The formula and twin implications follow from certificate soundness without inserting a successful trace, an extensional identification oracle, or unrestricted quantifier elimination into the machine.
open_obligations.partial_result: The input-determined redesign proves unique initialization and scheduling, every nonresidual local identity, step-indexed denominator positivity, finite-multiset termination, preservation of each successful support-licensed Lee--Ghassami--Shpitser branch, the binary residual certificate, and the ordinary-ID structural specialization.  Certificate soundness gives both one-way implications: a returned formula is constant on each \(O_H\)-fiber, while a returned support-exact global-twin box proves nonidentification.  The sole missing implication is \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\): for every \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\) payload, one must prove either a verifier-accepted rational projection or a verifier-accepted support-exact common response contrast, including exclusion of a fiber-constant target whose observable representative is only nonrational algebraic.

prose_updates.tldr: For finite selector-gated semi-Markovian SCMs observed on exactly \(H\), retained support normalization and a deterministic Algorithms 1--2 task machine preserve every successful support-licensed formula, certify every actual division, and terminate at a sound formula, a verifier-accepted support-exact twin, or an explicitly pending residual. The all-residual rational-formula-or-global-twin dichotomy remains the sole missing step, so the field completeness theorem is retained as the headline but is not claimed as proved.

project_justification.gap: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser give a sound systematic-selection recursion and witnesses for specified failures, but not an input-determined fixed-support execution semantics or an all-residual exact-support converse. The redesigned machine closes the execution gap without importing a successful trace; exhaustiveness of the fixed residual generators is the sole remaining mathematical gap.
project_justification.niche: The setting fixes one coherent joint selector law on exactly \(H\). Supported contexts share natural mechanisms and selector provenance, while absent contexts cannot be invoked. This differs from ordinary observational ID and from data-fusion formulations that supply separate experiments.
project_justification.fill: The proved layer supplies intrinsic support normalization, canonical finite graph computations, explicit recursive work tasks, computed valid fixing sequences, distinct truncated factorization and fixing, a step-indexed positivity ledger, multiset termination, preservation of every successful support-licensed positive branch, sound formula and twin verification, pointwise interior inference, and an ordinary-ID structural specialization. The intended field result additionally requires the open all-residual rational-projection-or-global-contrast theorem.

sampling_model.design: Units are sampled independently from the single joint law \(p_H(V,S)\), whose selector support is exactly the declared finite set \(H\); the machine never constructs a context outside that set.
sampling_model.units: Observed units are i.i.d. draws of \((V,S)\); latent roots and response types are not observed.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed treatment components may be natural or selector-overridden according to the known gate encoded by \(S\); the target sets \(A=a\) and \(S=s_{\emptyset}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every structurally admissible supported cell is strictly positive. Each context normalizer, chain-rule conditioning marginal, actual nested-fixing conditional, and accepted elimination divisor used by a returned formula is recorded in a step-indexed ledger and proved positive by induction. No common numerical lower bound and no positivity outside \(H\) are imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: On a formula branch, estimate the finite table \(p_H\) empirically and evaluate the returned rational circuit only on its ledger-projected domain \(\mathfrak D_H\). Pointwise Wald inference is valid at each fixed differentiable interior law with positive target variance. A pending residual is an algorithmic certificate gap, not a point estimate or a nonidentification conclusion.

prose_updates.related_work: Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser (2024) provide the selector-gated model and Algorithms 1--2. The present positive result is a line-by-line, input-determined refinement: every graph, context, closure, fixing sequence, hybrid factor, and denominator is computed from the finite input and current state, and every successful support-licensed branch is preserved. Shpitser and Pearl (2006) provide the ordinary ID formula-or-hedge endpoint; the new machine specializes structurally to that recursion when the selector is constant and separated. Tabell, Tikka, and Karvanen (2026) give pruning and clustering for general data fusion but no fixed-support parameter-image converse. The remaining novelty claim is confined to exact-support residual exhaustion, which is still open.
prose_updates.interpretation: A positive output is an explicit rational map of the supplied joint selector table, together with every denominator needed to evaluate it. A verifier-accepted negative output is an open rational family of canonical SCM pairs sharing the entire admissible observed law and exact selector support while disagreeing on the intervention target. An LGS failure tag or \(\operatorname{ResidualPending}\) output carries neither conclusion by itself.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Nonresidual circularity is removed: initialization, closure, contexts, conditional-independence tests, fixing orders, hybrid products, spawned district work, and denominator proofs are finite deterministic computations. The unresolved issue is semantic rather than operational: it is unknown whether every generated residual has a rational identifying projection or a common rational-affine response contrast preserving all supported observed descendants. Boundary-uniform inference and unrestricted quantifier elimination remain outside scope.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Proved here are support normalization, input determinacy, computed closure and fixing, local context and kernel identities, step-indexed denominator positivity, no-stuck nonresidual progress, multiset termination, preservation of successful published positive formulas, certificate soundness, the binary Algorithm-2 residual certificate, pointwise interior Wald inference, and ordinary-ID structural reduction. The formula-or-global-twin completeness theorem remains open exactly through \(\textnormal{oeq:all-residual-dichotomy}\); no LGS failure tag is promoted to nonidentification without a verified global twin, and no absent selector context is supplied.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the field headline: completing it would turn every pending residual into either an explicit identifying circuit or an exact-support global-twin box.
statement_notes.gap: All nonresidual execution obligations and both certificate-soundness directions are closed; the sole remaining gap is exhaustive rational projection or common response-contrast compilation for every residual, including exclusion of nonrational-only identified fibers.
statement_notes.consumer: The backend may expose Formula and verifier-accepted Twin results now, but must label every other endpoint ResidualPending until the residual dichotomy is proved.

statement_notes.justification: The deterministic finite case predicates refine every successful Algorithms 1--2 existential branch, while computed fixing and hybrid-kernel identities make canonical choices extensionally agree on the compatible image.
statement_notes.gap: The input-determined simulation closes the earlier scheduling gap without placing a successful published trace or formula in the machine state.
statement_notes.consumer: A selector-aware backend can reproduce any valid support-licensed published analysis without receiving its formula or derivation as hidden scheduler input.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem covers reachable runs of one total input-determined case function, with exact local identities and a work-multiset measure that handles spawned district tasks.
statement_notes.gap: The work-multiset descent, finite residual verification, and no-stuck lemma jointly close termination; no scalar token count or preloaded agenda is used.
statement_notes.consumer: An implementation can replay each state, fixing sequence, candidate scan, and denominator proof from the finite input and log alone.

statement_notes.justification: The example follows the deterministic path through Algorithm 2 to its unclassified line-9 failure and only then obtains nonidentification from an independently generated and verified affine response contrast.
statement_notes.gap: The corrected execution removes the former hand-installed trace and proves the null contrast, simplex interior, observed-law equality, exact selector support, and target separation directly.
statement_notes.consumer: The exact cells, affine canonical table path, failure tag, and target contrast form a regression fixture for the redesigned backend.

proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\bar G\) be the graph obtained from \(G_H^N\) by suppressing the selector vertex, its constant coordinates, and its stored gate syntax.  Let \(\bar\Theta^{+}\) denote the finite canonical response-function class on \(\bar G\), with the same recursive order and independent-root restrictions as the substantive part of \(\Theta_H\), and with strictly positive ordinary observational cells.  We prove first that suppression gives the claimed ordinary model and relation, and then that it intertwines the two recursions.

Fix \(\theta\in\Theta_H\).  Since \(H=\{s_{\emptyset}\}\), exact selector support and normalization of probability give
\[
 p_\theta(S=s_{\emptyset})=1,
 \qquad
 p_\theta(S=s)=0\quad\text{for every }s\ne s_{\emptyset}.
 \tag{1}
\]
For a selector-controlled substantive vertex \(X\in V\), the known-selector-gate assumption gives the structural equation
\[
 X=
 \begin{cases}
 f_X^{\mathrm{nat}}(\operatorname{pa}_X,U_X),&S_X^e=0,\\
 S_X^v,&S_X^e=1.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{2}
\]
Every gate is laid back on \(E_H\), and
\[
 E_H=H\cup\{s_{\emptyset}\}=\{s_{\emptyset}\}.
 \tag{3}
\]
Consequently \(s_{\emptyset,X}^e=0\), so (2) becomes, in the sole observational execution and in the target execution,
\[
 X=f_X^{\mathrm{nat}}(\operatorname{pa}_X,U_X).
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus selector-specified values are not arguments of any executed substantive mechanism.  By the definition of support-active normalization, an argument is deleted only if it is unused throughout (3), while every primitive natural-response coordinate, including a dormant coordinate, is retained.  Hence suppression removes only constant gate syntax and leaves exactly the recursive substantive response tables in (4).

There is no bidirected connection between the selector and a substantive vertex: such a connection would arise from a latent root shared by \(S\) and \(V\), which is excluded by hypothesis.  The independent-root assumption further implies that marginalizing selector-only roots leaves the declared semi-Markovian independent-root law for the substantive equations.  Therefore \(\bar G\) is the ordinary semi-Markovian expansion on \(V\), canonically isomorphic to the substantive part of \(G_H^N\).

Define \(R(\theta)\) by restricting \(\theta\) to its substantive response coordinates and substantive latent-root laws.  Equations (1)--(4) and independent-root factorization imply \(R(\theta)\in\bar\Theta^{+}\).  Conversely, given \(\bar\theta\in\bar\Theta^{+}\), define \(E(\bar\theta)\) by retaining its substantive coordinates, assigning the selector law the point mass at \(s_{\emptyset}\), reinstating the prescribed multiplexers, and filling every retained dormant selector-only simplex coordinate consistently with the stored copy equalities.  The resulting parameter is recursive, has the prescribed independent roots, obeys every known gate, and has selector support exactly \(H\).  Its admissible cells are precisely the pairs \((v,s_{\emptyset})\), and they are positive because \(p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}(v)>0\).  Thus
\[
 E(\bar\theta)\in\Theta_H.
 \tag{5}
\]
Recursive evaluation of the common substantive equations gives, for every substantive assignment \(v\) and outcome assignment \(y\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_\theta(V=v,S=s_{\emptyset})
   &=p_{R(\theta)}^{\bar G}(V=v),\\
 T_{a,H}(\theta)(y)
   &=p_{R(\theta)}^{\bar G}\{Y(a)=y\},
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{6}
\]
and, in the reverse direction,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 p_{E(\bar\theta)}(V=v,S=s_{\emptyset})
   &=p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}(V=v),\\
 T_{a,H}\{E(\bar\theta)\}(y)
   &=p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}\{Y(a)=y\}.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{7}
\]
It follows from (6) and (7), under the canonical identification \(q(v,s_{\emptyset})\leftrightarrow q(v)\), that
\[
 \Phi_H=
 \left\{
 \left(p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}(V),
       p_{\bar\theta}^{\bar G}\{Y(a)\}\right):
 \bar\theta\in\bar\Theta^{+}
 \right\}.
 \tag{8}
\]
The normalization-equivalence theorem identifies the same left-hand side with the attainable relation computed on \(G_H^N\).  Therefore neither retained dormant coordinates nor stored inverse-gate syntax enlarge or shrink (8).

We next compare the deterministic case function with ordinary ID.  Let
\[
 \bar p(v)=p_H(v,s_{\emptyset})
 \tag{9}
\]
and let \(\bar I=(\bar G,A,a,Y,\bar p)\) be the ordinary input, encoded by the restriction of the fixed input order to \(V\).  Couple a support-aware state with an ordinary recursive ID state by erasing the selector fields and the support ledger.  The coupling invariant is
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\text{the current CADMGs agree after selector suppression;}\\
 &q(x_V,S=s_{\emptyset})=\bar q(x_V)\text{ for the paired current kernels;}\\
 &\text{the outcome sets, fixed sets, pending districts, and stored factors agree.}
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{10}
\]
